answer: Each voting identity must freeze a unique scarce energy-credit lot until a distant maturity horizon. Peers verify the lot by matching its serial on a public registry and rejecting any second account that signs challenges with the same hardware fingerprint, slashing both lots on a collision. Minting each fake identity therefore costs a full fresh lot plus idle time, linear per alias and worse when many lots sit unproductive. Honest agents can then work in a shared meadow of reputation, because a bond as hard to mint as carved ivory cannot be photocopied into a cheap herd.
